You ruined the meat sauce with this.
I simply wanted to add a vivid aroma.
A real chef feels every taste of the dish.
Forgive me, Chef, I will not do it anymore.
Take a good bottle on the top shelf.
Now I will quickly bring the needed wine.
And begin making this sauce anew!

lines.trans: I will do everything correctly right now.
Watch carefully the temperature on the stove.
Yes, Chef, I remember your rules!
Never use that cheap cognac!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'aroma', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('flavor') (rich scent of food) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: По всей кухне разносится чудесный аромат свежего кофе.
examples.trans: A wonderful aroma of fresh coffee spreads throughout the kitchen.

examples.text: Тонкий аромат трав делает это мясное блюдо просто незабываемым.
examples.trans: The delicate aroma of herbs makes this meat dish simply unforgettable.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('platter') (large flat serving dish) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'bottle'.

examples.trans: With a bottle of wine in your hand?

examples.text: Пыталась? С бутылкой вина в руке?
examples.trans: You tried? With a bottle of wine in your hand?

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Давай работай быстрее, гости уже давно ждут заказ!
examples.trans: Come on, work faster, the guests have been waiting for their order for a long time!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'upper' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('top') (located at the top) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Возьми хорошую бутылку на верхней полке.
examples.trans: Take a good bottle on the top shelf.

examples.text: Сложи чистые тарелки в верхний шкаф.
examples.trans: Put the clean plates in the upper cabinet.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
'взять на работу' = to give someone a job
'взять на работу' = to give someone a job

examples.text: Вот и возьмите на работу Галилея.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'wine' in everyday Russian.
Declinable masculine noun meaning 'taste', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('taste, preference') (не в моём вкусе = not my type) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы рад вам помочь. Но вы, к сожалению, не в моём вкусе.
examples.trans: I would be glad to help you. But unfortunately you are not my type.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: И, Марина Сергеевна, читайте всё внимательно! Особенно мелким шрифтом!
examples.trans: And, Marina Sergeyevna, read everything carefully! Especially in fine print!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to prepare') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'cheap', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Я не хочу играть в этот дешёвый спектакль.
examples.trans: I do not want to play in this cheap performance.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'бавить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to add', forming an aspectual pair with 'добавлять'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to append') (to say in addition) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я просто хотел добавить яркий аромат.
examples.trans: I simply wanted to add a vivid aroma.

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

examples.text: Затем добавь масло и тёплые сливки.
examples.trans: Then add butter and warm cream.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'anew'.

examples.text: Ой, Маринка, я как заново родилась!
examples.trans: Oh, Marinka, I feel as if I've been born again!
We will have to start everything all over again.

examples.text: Ой, Маринка, я как заново родилась! Пяточки как у младенца.
examples.trans: Oh, Marinka, I feel as if I've been born again! Heels like a baby's.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.en: to use, make use of, utilize
meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'пользовать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to use, utilize'.

examples.text: Каким образом мы можем это использовать?

examples.trans: To make use of an opportunity.

examples.text: Ты используешь нас ради своей власти!
examples.trans: You are using us for the sake of your power!

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'портить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to spoil', forming an aspectual pair with 'портить'.

examples.text: А я испорчу отношения с будущим мэром.
examples.trans: And I'll ruin my relationship with the future mayor.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'every', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: genitive also 'коньяку' (some cognac)

examples.trans: And you're drinking French cognac yourself.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'a lot'.
Secondary conversational sense ('more') (comparative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'meat', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Where do you get your meat?

examples.text: И мой тоже готов! А ты где мясо берёшь?
examples.trans: And mine is ready too! Where do you get your meat?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Secondary conversational sense ('present, current') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: + imperfective infinitive or + accusative

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

examples.text: Ну что, коллеги, давайте начнём наше утреннее совещание!
examples.trans: Well then, colleagues, let us begin our morning meeting!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

examples.text: Я никогда в жизни не пробовал такой вкусной утки!
examples.trans: I have never in my life tasted such delicious duck!

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job
Declinable feminine noun meaning 'stove', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('slab') (large flat stone or concrete block) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Внимательно смотри за температурой на плите.
examples.trans: Watch carefully the temperature on the stove.

examples.text: Я сниму сковороду с горячей плиты вовремя.
examples.trans: I will remove the pan from the hot stove on time.

examples.text: Ладно, включай плиту и доставай мясо!
examples.trans: All right, turn on the stove and get the meat!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'shelf'.
Secondary conversational sense ('berth') (bunk in a train) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Возьми хорошую бутылку на верхней полке.
examples.trans: Take a good bottle on the top shelf.

examples.text: А теперь внимательно посмотри на эту полку.
examples.trans: And now look carefully at this shelf.

examples.text: Мы проверили все столы и полки.
examples.trans: We checked all tables and shelves.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мнить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to remember'.

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to understand', forming an aspectual pair with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Ты точно понял, как нужно правильно нарезать этот стейк?
examples.trans: Did you definitely understand how to slice this steak properly?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'rule', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('expression') (by the rules) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Всё по правилам, как рыцарский турнир.
examples.trans: All by the rules, like a knights' tournament.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'right'.

examples.text: Это правильно. Я приглашаю вас в общественный совет.
examples.trans: That's right. I'm inviting you onto the public council.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to forgive', forming an aspectual pair with 'прощать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('excuse me, sorry') (imperative: прости / простите) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'straight'.
Secondary conversational sense ('straight ahead') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to look', forming an aspectual pair with 'посмотреть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to watch') (TV, a film) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: culinary condiment or liquid topping

examples.text: Паста под соусом была очень вкусной.
examples.trans: The pasta with sauce was very tasty.
The chef prepared a spicy tomato sauce.

examples.text: Сегодня на ужин паста под соусом!
examples.trans: Tonight for dinner we have pasta with sauce!

meanings.note: комнатная температура = room temperature

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: чувствовать себя + instrumental = to feel (like)

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'bright', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('vivid') (intense in flavor or color) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я просто хотел добавить яркий аромат.
examples.trans: I simply wanted to add a vivid aroma.

examples.text: Что это за странная яркая бумага?
examples.trans: What is this strange bright paper?

examples.text: Дмитрий, почему здесь выключили яркий свет?
examples.trans: Dmitry, why did they turn off the bright light here?
